titre: What to do if the other parent does not pay child support (ARIPA)
resume: Unpaid or late child support: the exact documents to ask the Caf (ARIPA) to recover the money and pay you the support every month, what to do if you have no enforceable order, and the ASF as a top-up.
aQuoiCaSert: With financial intermediation, the Caf (Caisse d'allocations familiales, the family benefits office), through its ARIPA agency (Agence de recouvrement et d'intermédiation des pensions alimentaires, the child support collection agency), collects the support every month from the paying parent and passes it on to you. If payments are missed, it starts recovery, free of charge for you. To act, it needs an enforceable order (titre exécutoire) setting the amount of support. In the meantime, the family support allowance (allocation de soutien familial, ASF) can be paid to you in advance.
quiEstConcerne: The parent who is owed child support and does not receive it, receives only part of it, or receives it late.
Separated parents, married or not. You do not need to be a Caf beneficiary, and the other parent's agreement is not required.
Not covered: support paid directly to an adult child, between former spouses (compensatory allowance, prestation compensatoire) or to grandparents.
aSavoir: You need an enforceable order: a judgment of the family court judge (juge aux affaires familiales, JAF), an agreement approved by the judge, a divorce by mutual consent agreement (lawyers and notary), a notarial deed, a mediation or conciliation agreement bearing the enforcement clause, or an order issued by the Caf or the MSA (Mutualité sociale agricole, the farmers' social security fund).

No enforceable order: if you are not married and agree on the amount, ask the Caf together for an enforceable order (paper form signed by both parents). If you do not agree, apply to the family court judge.
If your order provides for intermediation, you have nothing to do: the court registry (greffe), lawyer or notary sends it to ARIPA. Otherwise, apply online.
ARIPA makes its first payment no later than 60 days after receiving all the documents. In the meantime, support is still paid directly between the parents.
Free for both parents. If payments are missed, the non-paying parent bears fees of 7.5% (amicable recovery) or 10% (enforced recovery).
Domestic violence: intermediation is mandatory and cannot be stopped, even by mutual agreement.
Arrears: support can be claimed for up to 5 years back. Through a judicial officer (commissaire de justice), direct payment only recovers the last 6 months.
In addition, the ASF (€200.78 per child per month) is paid in advance if the set support is not paid: see the guide entry "Family support allowance (ASF, allocation de soutien familial)".

documents.detail: Judgment, approved agreement, divorce agreement, notarial deed or Caf order. If you have lost it, ask the court registry, the lawyer or the notary for a copy.
Account into which ARIPA will pay the support.

documents.libelle: Known contact details of the other parent
documents.detail: Name, date of birth, last known address, employer if you know it. They help ARIPA reach them.

documents.libelle: Table of unpaid amounts and proof
documents.detail: Month by month: amount due, amount received, date. Bank statements, written exchanges, reminder letter. The Lien Parental Journal can help you prepare it.

documents.libelle: Caf or MSA beneficiary number, if you have one
Copy of the reminder letter to the other parent
documents.detail: Optional: a template letter is available on service-public.gouv.fr.
Including the letter stating the start date of intermediation.

etapes.titre: Gather proof of the missed payments
etapes.detail: List month by month what is due and what was received. You can first send a written reminder to the other parent.

etapes.titre: Check that you have an enforceable order
etapes.detail: No order: ask for a Caf order if you agree on the amount (unmarried parents), otherwise apply to the family court judge. Apply for the ASF at the same time.

Legible, complete copy of the enforceable order (all pages); ID document; bank details (RIB) in your name; the other parent's contact details; table of missed payments with proof. Keep a copy of everything.
Application for financial intermediation and recovery. ARIPA then writes to each parent; reply quickly and keep your information up to date in your account.

etapes.titre: Apply to the Caf for the ASF if support is not paid
etapes.detail: It is paid in advance during recovery.

etapes.titre: Track each payment in the Journal
etapes.detail: With the proof. Lien Parental does not certify that a payment was made, but helps you keep a record.

Judicial officer (direct payment, seizure), recovery by the Public Treasury through the public prosecutor after another procedure has failed, or a criminal complaint for family abandonment (abandon de famille) after more than 2 months of non-payment. A lawyer or a point-justice (free legal information center) can advise you.

ou.detail: Online application for intermediation and recovery, child support simulator. Advisers available Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (numbers on the "Nous contacter" page).
ASF application and sending the Caf enforceable order form.

Legal information; legal aid (aide juridictionnelle) may be available depending on your income.

aConfirmer: The exact list of documents ARIPA requires is not published: it may ask for additional documents while processing your application.
ARIPA does not state the processing time for a Caf enforceable order request.
How far back arrears are recovered under the ASF and Caf recovery should be confirmed with ARIPA for your situation.
